deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 10–12). These are preparatory notes for Grothendieck's Nov.–Dec. 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, later written up as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968).

Setup. M^· is an object of D^+(X/S): a bounded-below complex of O_X-modules whose differentials are differential operators relative to S. Q°[M^·] is its linearization. In each degree it is the pro-object P^∞_{X/S} ⊗ M^i, the formal completion of the diagonal tensored with M^i. These are (pro-)O_X-modules carrying a stratification, and the differentials have become O_X-linear and horizontal.

Hypotheses. One wants the cohomology sheaves H^i(ℓQ°[M^·]) to commute with the cosimplicial base changes along the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal (the cosimplicial pro-scheme X^{[·]}). This is to be ensured by flatness conditions on Q°[M^·] and on its H^i. Grothendieck remarks that flatness of Q°[M^·] over O_X essentially forces a hypothesis on X^{[1]} → X. He calls it 'platitude différentielle de X/S': flatness of the first-order (or infinitesimal) neighbourhood of the diagonal over X, e.g. X/S smooth. He notes that a precise criterion still has to be extracted ('critère : dégager').

Conclusions.
(1) V^i = H^i(ℓQ°[M^·]) are O_X-modules (via the left O_X-structure) with a natural stratification.
(2) Form the bicomplex ℓQ*[M^·]: the linearization of M^· combined with the de Rham/Čech–Alexander resolution in the stratification direction. Taking first the cohomology along the differential operators coming from M^· gives the de Rham (stratification) complexes C^·(V^i) attached to the stratified modules V^i.
(3) Hence a spectral sequence (next page):
H^*(X, M^·) ≅ H^*(X, Q*[M^·]) ⇐ E_2^{pq} = H^p_str(X, V^q(M^·)).
Its degenerate case is the corollary: if V^q = 0 for q ≠ q0, then H^n(X, M^·) ≅ H^{n−q0}_str(X, V^{q0}).

In modern terms: the linearization equivalence H^*(X, M^·) ≅ H^*_crys/str(X, L(M^·)) (Grothendieck, Berthelot Ch. IV), followed by the spectral sequence of the canonical filtration of L(M^·). This is the mechanism behind constructing Gauss–Manin-type stratifications on cohomology sheaves (cf. Katz–Oda).
errors: Gap acknowledged by Grothendieck himself: the flatness conditions guaranteeing that H^i(ℓQ°[M]) commutes with the cosimplicial base change are not specified ('critère : dégager').
Identifying H^*(X, M^·) with H^*(X, Q*[M^·]) needs the linearization/Poincaré-lemma comparison; here it is only asserted (the next page asks 'vérif. à EGA 0_III ?'). It is correct in the smooth case.
Grothendieck notes on p.10 that the stratified structure does not fully remember the O_X-structures; this does not affect the spectral sequence.

ideas.what: Linearization of a complex of differential operators into a complex of stratified pro-modules, and comparison of hypercohomologies
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p_str(X, H^q(L(M^·))) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, M^·), with a degeneration corollary
ideas.modern_name: Spectral sequence of the canonical filtration on the linearized complex (Gauss–Manin / Leray-type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Katz–Oda (1968) for the Gauss–Manin version; Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Dix exposés; unsure

ideas.what: 'Platitude différentielle' of X/S: flatness of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal over X, as the hypothesis needed for base change of the linearized cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Close to the 'différentiellement lisse' hypothesis (P^n flat) of EGA IV 16.10

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags a need for a precise flatness criterion, weaker than smoothness ('platitude différentielle'), under which the cohomology sheaves of the linearized complex are stratified and commute with base change. The literature essentially always assumes smoothness instead.
missed.quote: une hypothèse de "platitude différentielle de X/S" ... p.ex. X/S lisse ----- [ critère : dégager ]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It could matter for linearization and crystalline comparison over non-smooth bases or for singular X, but modern derived and prismatic approaches largely bypass this.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material of the 1967 crystals lectures (linearization and the associated spectral sequence). The only unpublished nuance is the 'differential flatness' hypothesis with an explicitly unfinished criterion.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the inserted word above 'platitude' is 'type' ('de type platitude sur les Q°[M·] et les H^i(Q°(M·))'). The symbol is Q° throughout (the previous page's 'C°' is likely the same Q°).
'X^{[1]} → X^0' should probably read 'X^{[1]} → X' (the second occurrence clearly has no superscript). The marginal insertion reads 'une hyp. de platitude sur X^{[1]} → X'.
'Les V^i = H^i(ℓQ°[M]) sont des ... faisceaux naturels': 'naturels' is uncertain; it could be 'munis naturellement'. 'stratifiés' is underlined.
The line before 'des V^i' is uncertain. 'de de Rham' is not clearly legible: 'complexes' is inserted above a struck word, and 'stratifications' replaces the struck-out 'connexions'.
